title: Explore the attempts and shape the activity columns
prompt:
The learning team wants to know who is making progress, which courses get finished and who has gone quiet. Everything starts from the platform's activity export: `attempts`, one row per try at a lesson, beside the `learners`, `courses` and `lessons` tables in the project data. Look at it first. Add `attempts.printSchema()` and `print(attempts.count())` inside the function and press Run.

Then write `attempt_view(attempts)`. It returns the columns the reports use, in order, plus `activity_date`: the calendar day of `started_at`. Every row stays: this step only shapes the columns.
rules: `activity_date` is the day of `started_at`, as a date. An attempt with no start time has no `activity_date`.
Every row of `attempts` is still there, repeated and odd rows included.
hints: `select` picks columns in the order you list them; `minutes_spent` isn't one of them.
`F.to_date("started_at")` turns a timestamp into its day. Name it with `.alias("activity_date")`.
Don't filter yet: the next step decides which attempts count.
explanation: `select` both chooses and orders the columns, and `F.to_date("started_at").alias("activity_date")` adds the day each attempt started, as a real date. Later steps compare days, not times of day, so having that column once, in the first function, keeps every report using the same day. Nothing is filtered: the export's repeated and broken rows are dealt with, and counted, in the next steps.
